title: Deep learning identifies previously unreported protein interactions in human bacterial pathogens
summary: A RoseTTAFold2-Lite pipeline combined residue coevolution, deep-learning complex prediction and AlphaFold modelling to screen protein pairs across 19 human bacterial pathogens. In a validation set selected using the deep-learning pipeline, co-immunoprecipitation detected four of six predicted interactions. Three pairs lacked prior direct interaction evidence: E. coli UbiE–YcaR, P. aeruginosa PA4105–PA4106, and P. aeruginosa WbpG–HisF2. The PA4105–PA4106 structural similarity to proteins in 3-thiaglutamate biosynthesis and the WbpG–HisF2 result provide functional hypotheses, not established native-pathogen mechanisms.
ai_technology: RoseTTAFold2-Lite integrated with direct coupling analysis and AlphaFold complex modelling
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design; University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center; Broad Institute; Massachusetts General Hospital; University of Connecticut; Seoul National University; collaborating institutions

evidence.tested: In a validation set selected using the deep-learning pipeline, co-immunoprecipitation detected four of six predicted interactions.
evidence.unknown: The positive interaction evidence comes from heterologous co-immunoprecipitation/pull-down assays, with two independent experiments per positive pair, rather than native-pathogen systems. The validation subset was small (four positives among six AI-selected candidates); most of the thousands of predicted interactions remain untested, and false positives and false negatives are expected. Proposed roles for PA4105–PA4106 and UbiE–YcaR remain hypotheses; this paper does not establish their physiological function or a therapeutic target.
evidence.ai_role: RoseTTAFold2-Lite used residue–residue coevolution and predicted complex structures to rank candidate protein pairs in a proteome-wide screen. The authors selected six pairs from the final deep-learning pipeline for co-immunoprecipitation tests; four yielded positive interaction signals. Three were described as lacking previously reported direct interaction evidence, including UbiE–YcaR, PA4105–PA4106 and WbpG–HisF2. The models enabled the experimental target selection; they did not themselves establish physical interactions.
